    • limitBuy

      public OrderExecutionResult<?> limitBuy(BigDecimal amount, BigDecimal price, org.knowm.xchange.instrument.Instrument instrument, Collection<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order.IOrderFlags> flags)
      Places a limit buy order after adjusting the price to the instrument's price scale and computing the counter-currency amount. Validates that the resulting counter amount meets the exchange minimum; throws if it does not.
      Parameters:
      amount - the base amount to buy
      price - the desired limit price (will be rounded to instrument precision)
      instrument - the trading instrument (e.g., BTC/USDT)
      flags - optional order flags (FOK, IOC, GTC, etc.)
      Returns:
      the order execution result containing the order ID or error

      public OrderExecutionResult<?> stopSell(BigDecimal amount, BigDecimal price, BigDecimal stopPrice, Instrument instrument, StopIntention intention, org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple.Pair<String,Object>... extraParams)
      Places a stop sell order using the engine-canonical StopIntention enum. Converts the intention to the XChange equivalent at this boundary.
      Parameters:
      amount - the base amount to sell
      price - the limit price for stop-limit, or null for stop-market
      stopPrice - the trigger price
      instrument - the engine-canonical trading instrument
      intention - the engine-canonical stop intention
      Returns:
      the order execution result

    • stopOrder

      public OrderExecutionResult<?> stopOrder(org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order.OrderType orderType, BigDecimal amount, BigDecimal price, BigDecimal stopPrice, org.knowm.xchange.instrument.Instrument instrument, org.knowm.xchange.dto.trade.StopOrder.Intention intention, org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple.Pair<String,Object>... extraParams)
      Places a stop order (stop-loss or stop-limit) after adjusting prices to instrument precision. If price is null, creates a stop-market order; otherwise creates a stop-limit order. Validates that the counter amount meets the exchange minimum.
      Parameters:
      orderType - BID (buy) or ASK (sell)
      amount - the base amount
      price - the limit price for stop-limit, or null for stop-market
      stopPrice - the trigger/stop price
      instrument - the trading instrument
      intention - the stop order intention (e.g., STOP_LOSS, TAKE_PROFIT)
      extraParams - additional exchange-specific parameters
      Returns:
      the order execution result containing the order ID or error

    • createObservableOrderExecution

      public io.reactivex.rxjava3.core.Observable<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order> createObservableOrderExecution(org.knowm.xchange.instrument.Instrument instrument, Callable<OrderExecutionResult<?>> orderExecutor)

    • createObservableOrderExecution

      public io.reactivex.rxjava3.core.Observable<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order> createObservableOrderExecution(org.knowm.xchange.instrument.Instrument instrument, io.reactivex.rxjava3.core.Scheduler scheduler, Callable<OrderExecutionResult<?>> orderExecutor)
      Creates an Observable that places an order and monitors its lifecycle via WebSocket order change events. The flow works as follows:
      1. Subscribes to the instrument's order changes stream before placing the order
      2. Executes the order via the provided callable
      3. Uses a CountDownLatch to synchronize the order ID between the execution thread and the filter predicate on the order changes stream
      4. Emits the exchange's own answer to the placement — the acknowledged order, or the refused one when the exchange declined it — so the subscriber holds the order's server-side identity and outcome even if no event ever follows
      5. Filters order changes to only pass through events matching the placed order's ID
      6. Completes the observable when the order reaches a final status (FILLED, CANCELLED, etc.)
      This coordination pattern handles the race condition where order change events may arrive before the order placement returns the order ID.
      Parameters:
      instrument - the instrument being traded
      scheduler - the RxJava scheduler for observing order changes
      orderExecutor - callable that places the order and returns the execution result
      Returns:
      an Observable emitting order status updates until the order reaches a final state
